_: Adjudication for tools/check-ordered-closure.mjs. Every crossing the reachability census finds must be converted or listed here with a reason; every place the census cannot see must be listed in `opaque`. An entry that no longer matches anything FAILS the gate — a stale exclusion is how a converted-away reason outlives the thing it excused.

crossings.Ampd.AuthorityCoordinator.observe/2 -> A: ENTERING the order is not a crossing INSIDE it. All three coordinator entries test `self() == Process.whereis(__MODULE__)` first and run the closure directly when they are already the total order, so this call is only ever made from outside, where a `GenServer.call` exit is the caller's own business.
crossings.Ampd.AuthorityCoordinator.observe_once/2: As above. Reached in the census only through the imprecise root at `Ampd.Projection.ordered_observe/2`, which forwards a closure it received.
crossings.Ampd.AuthorityCoordinator.transact/3 ->: As above, and re-entrancy is measured rather than assumed: `transact/3` line 171 runs `fun.()` directly when the caller IS the coordinator. `Ampd.Carrier` deliberately opens a NEW transaction from outside one (`start/2`, `settle_commit/3`) and that is the outside case.
crossings.Ampd.Bootstrap.close_all!/0 -> ?_tab@1 :: MEASURED (probes/boundary_primitives.exs): `:dets.close` on a table that is not open returns `{:error, :not_owner}` and the caller LIVES. This site also pre-checks `:dets.info(tab) == :undefined` before every attempt.
crossings.Ampd.Store.seed!/2 -> ?_tab@1 :: :dets.c: MEASURED: `:dets.close` cannot exit its caller. Same evidence as `Ampd.Bootstrap.close_all!/0`.
crossings.Ampd.Store.open/1 -> ?_tab@1 :: :dets.op: Reached inside the order only from `Ampd.Bootstrap.new_world!/0` under `reset_world!/0`, which is an operator/fixture path (`Ampd.reset!/0`, `Ampd.TestFixture`) and NOT reachable from any `Ampd.CommandSpec` command. `open!/1` already raises there by design — world initialization over a damaged store is fatal, stated in its own docstring — and a class cannot change that.
crossings.Ampd.Store.save/2 -> ?_tab@1 :: :dets.in: MEASURED: `:dets.insert` on a closed table or one whose server died RAISES `badarg` and the caller DIES. That matters, and the boundary now covers it: every production path reaches `Ampd.Store.save/2` inside a registry participant's `handle_call`, and that participant's death is exactly what `Ampd.Participant` classifies — `:indeterminate` for a mutation. The only path that reaches it in the coordinator itself is `new_world!/0`, on a table opened three lines above, where a failure is the fatal world-init case above.
crossings.Ampd.Store.save/2 -> ?_tab@1 :: :dets.sy: As `:dets.insert/2` above, same call, same two lines.
crossings.Ampd.Carrier.Reaper.orphaned/1 -> Ampd.C: MEASURED: `GenServer.cast/2` returns `:ok` for an absent name, a dead name and a dead pid, and never exits the caller. It also cannot report delivery, so there is no outcome for a class to describe — it is a notification, not an operation.
crossings.Ampd.RefusalLog.record/1 -> Ampd.Refusal: MEASURED cast, as above. Reached from 16 roots because `Ampd.Refusal.new/2` records as it constructs; converting it would put a synchronous crossing on every refusal in the tree.
crossings.Ampd.Subscriptions.changed/0 -> Ampd.Sub: MEASURED cast, as above, and deliberately asynchronous: `Ampd.AuthorityCoordinator` documents at `applied/2` that a synchronous notification from inside the order would let a subscriber's rebuild re-enter the coordinator that is still holding the transaction.
crossings.Ampd.Carrier.Machine.Gate.call/1 -> Ampd: ALREADY A LOCAL BOUNDARY, of the right shape. The catch is narrow and named (`catch :exit, _` around exactly one primitive, not around a caller-supplied closure) and its `{:error, why}` is consumed by `Ampd.Carrier` as INDETERMINATE at both call sites — `carrier-start-indeterminate` and `carrier-reconcile-indeterminate`, neither retried, neither duplicated. RESIDUAL, stated: a `:noproc` there is reported as `did not answer in time`, so a provably-never-delivered start is classified INDETERMINATE rather than NOT_APPLIED. That is conservative in the safe direction — it over-claims unknown — and narrowing it would change `Ampd.Carrier`'s attempt grammar, which is not this slice.
crossings.Ampd.TerminalAttachment.snapshot/2 -> ?_: ALREADY A LOCAL BOUNDARY via `Ampd.Carrier.Terminal.safely/1`, and it must stay one: `safely/1` maps a timeout to `:unreachable` because for THIS participant a timeout is information — measured in D.1.3c·2b·1, exactly one phase can fail to answer in time, so a busy owner is an ACTIVE owner. `Ampd.Participant` would discard that by classifying the same timeout `:unavailable`. This is a read; nothing is mutated. The MUTATION on the same participant (`activate`) is converted — see `Ampd.Carrier.Terminal.finalise_stream/4`.

opaque.Ampd.AuthorityCoordinator.classify/1 fun: The transaction closure itself. This IS the root the census starts from — every caller-supplied `fn` is enumerated at its own call site, so the fun value here is already accounted for on the other side.
opaque.Ampd.AuthorityCoordinator.observe/2 fun_: Re-entrant branch: the caller already IS the order, so the closure is one the census enumerated at its own site.
opaque.Ampd.Bootstrap.close_all!/0 computed_rem: `reg.close_store()` where `reg` comes from `registry_for/1`, a total function over a literal list of eight registry modules. All eight are converted; `close_store` is declared `:mutate` in every one.
opaque.Ampd.Bootstrap.reload_registries!/0 comp: `registry_for(name).load_state(s)`, the same eight modules. `load_state` is declared `:mutate` in every one.
opaque.Ampd.Bootstrap.complaint/2 computed_call: A formatting fun applied to a field list. Reaches no process.
opaque.Ampd.Carrier.execution_basis/0 computed_: `machine().execution_basis()` — the `Ampd.Carrier.Machine` behaviour. Production dispatches to `Ampd.Carrier.Machine.Channel`, which reaches `Ampd.Bridge.carrier_endpoint/0` (converted, `:read`). The other implementation is `Ampd.Carrier.Machine.Harness`, a test double that reaches no process.
opaque.Ampd.Carrier.Floor.safe/2 fun_value: A guard applied to a floor predicate. The predicates it is given reach no process.
opaque.Ampd.Carrier.Terminal.safely/1 fun_value: The narrow named catch declared above. Its two call sites are literal and both are accounted for.
opaque.Ampd.Control.settled/2 fun_value: A result-shaping continuation applied to an already-computed value. Reaches no process.
opaque.Ampd.Gateway.perform/5 fun_value: The effect adapter. `Ampd.Gateway.perform/4` runs AFTER `claim_and_consume/4` returns and is therefore outside the order; the census reaches it only through the conservative whole-`dispatch/3` admission at `Ampd.Control.in_lineage/4`.
opaque.Ampd.Locus.observe/2 fun_value: A projection shaper applied to an already-read worktree resource.
opaque.Ampd.Projection.agent/1 fun_value: `mine`, the per-actor filter, applied to lists already read from the participants above it.
opaque.Ampd.Terminal.Presentation.occupancy/1 f: The `Enum.find_value/2` predicate over `Ampd.Peer.attachments/0`. It reaches exactly two things and the census resolves both from other call sites: `Ampd.Peer.resolve/1` (converted, `:read`) and `Ampd.Worker.occupancy_of/3` (a pure derivation over the attachment, the peer and the lane — it reaches no process of its own).

_removed_D_1_3C_2C_1A: REMOVED, and the gate is what found it. This excused `Ampd.TerminalAttachment.state/2` as an ordered crossing because `Ampd.Terminal.Presentation.status_of/1` reached it from `Ampd.Worker.projected/1`, which the operator projection builds inside an ordered observation. The A2 repair split the chain: `status_of/1` now runs the semantic derivation only, and the stream probe is reached from `resolve/3` alone — which no wire command calls yet. So the crossing is gone and the exclusion excused nothing, which is exactly the shape this file's `_` warns about. It comes back, with a reason written against the then-current source, if and when D.1.3c·2c·1b puts `resolve/3` on an ordered path. The prior reason read: ALREADY A LOCAL BOUNDARY via `Ampd.Carrier.Terminal.stream_phase/1`, which wraps it in `safely/1` — the same narrow named catch, on the same participant, for the same measured reason as `snapshot` above: a timeout there means the owner is BUSY, and busy is ACTIVE. `Ampd.Participant` would classify that timeout `:unavailable` and discard the one fact it carries. Newly reachable inside the order as of D.1.3c·2c·1a: `Ampd.Terminal.Presentation.status_of/1` is called from `Ampd.Worker.projected/1`, which the operator projection builds inside an ordered observation. This is a read; nothing is mutated.
